prompt:
Act as a brutally skeptical novelty reviewer. Evaluate two versions of an idea for a top-tier paper on efficient on-policy distillation (OPD).

Version A (naive): port Curvature-Aware Policy Optimization (CAPO; Melo et al., ICLR 2026, arXiv:2510.00819) to sampled-token / RL-style OPD. Use a sparse last-LM-layer model to estimate prospective Hessian objective shift m_H and Fisher/KL policy shift m_F for each token, mask destabilizing token updates, then train with a higher learning rate and smaller batch to reduce teacher-scored completions and wall-clock to target quality.

Version B (OPD-specific): diagnose that existing OPD filters conflate two axes: teacher-signal reliability (is the teacher correction valid/reachable on this student prefix?) and optimization safety (would applying this otherwise useful correction induce a destructive policy shift?). Build a two-axis router using teacher/student support or verifier evidence for reliability and prospective Hessian/Fisher geometry for update safety. Preserve high-disagreement but useful tokens; soften or defer reliable-but-curvature-dangerous tokens; redirect or mask unreliable tokens. Derive the curvature model for the actual OPD objective, explicitly handling sampled-token bias and student-dependent log-ratio rewards rather than reusing the RLVR proof unchanged. Claim efficiency only if this permits an aggressive LR/small-batch regime and reduces teacher-scored completions/GPU-hours at matched performance.

CAPO facts: standard setup LR 3e-6, batch 1152; aggressive setup LR 1.5e-5, batch 96. CAPO uses token-level Hessian/Fisher estimates in a top-k sparse last-layer model and masks tokens; it reports 30x fewer completions on MATH, 9x on TEST, <8% early and <2% later rejection, 2.94% step-time overhead and about 2GB transient memory on 4xH100. The gain is sample efficiency enabled by aggressive optimization, not 30x faster rollout throughput.

Closest literature found through 2026-08-25:
- CAPO, ICLR 2026: exact curvature-aware masking mechanism in RLVR.
- Trust Region On-Policy Distillation / TrOPD, arXiv:2606.01249: teacher/student likelihood-ratio trust region; token partition; outliers use top-k FKL; teacher-prefix guidance.
- Trust Region Policy Distillation / TOP-D, arXiv:2607.04751: proximal teacher bounds reward variance, internal off-policy reuse, monotonic improvement, sample efficiency, zero added overhead.
- REOPOLD, ICML 2026, arXiv:2603.11137: reward clipping, entropy token sampling, exploration-to-refinement schedule.
- Revisiting OPD, arXiv:2603.25562: sampled-token bias/variance, support mismatch, top-k local RKL, top-p rollout and masking.
- KL for a KL / vOPD, ICML submission 2026: closed-form negative-RKL control variate; matches full-vocab OPD with up to 57.7% wall-clock reduction.
- OPD+, arXiv:2606.01039: student-dependent reward and stop-gradient objective bias.
- StableOPD, arXiv:2604.08527: reference divergence plus rollout mixture prevents repetition/length collapse.
- EffOPD, arXiv:2605.11739: parameter-direction extrapolation, about 3x training acceleration.
- Prune-OPD / full-rollout / Adaptive FastOPD: reduce rollout/scoring tokens or horizon, up to roughly 49-71% time reduction in Adaptive FastOPD.
- FP-OPD, arXiv:2608.01263: Fisher-projected OPD for locally realizable visual corrections; Fisher geometry already appears in OPD, but for capacity-aware target projection rather than update stability.
- On the Geometry of OPD and Dense Supervision, Sparse Updates, arXiv 2026: post-hoc update/subspace geometry.
- PGPO, HiLD 2026 workshop: physics/Fisher-like modulation for self-distilled policy optimization; verify conceptual overlap based on provided summary only.

Please answer: (1) novelty and publishability of A and B separately, (2) closest prior work and exact delta, (3) whether CAPO's mathematical assumptions survive OPD rewards, (4) what single falsifiable mechanism finding is needed beyond an X-to-Y port, (5) minimum experiment matrix and kill criteria suitable for an 8-16 GPU academic budget. Give 0-10 novelty scores and a PROCEED / PROCEED WITH CAUTION / ABANDON verdict. Do not be polite; identify likely reviewer rejection language.
